name: go-backend-phase3-contract-matrix
scope: Narrator plan mode, compact/retry/recovery, foreground/background subagents, MCP tool discovery versus agent injection, and review tool closure.

features: /api/narrators/:id/plan stores and retrieves plan state
plan-mode enter/exit persists planMode and previous permission mode traits
EnterPlanMode and ExitPlanMode tools are available through the reflection tool scope
ExitPlanMode persists an approved compact plan marker when invoked by the agent runtime

ExitPlanMode always requires explicit user approval after readiness reflection; Go does not implement the TS planReflectionAutoApprove skip-user path, so the TS auto-compact reflection sub-feature (planReflectionAllowAutoCompact / ExitPlanConfirmAndCompact / confirm_compact) is an accepted divergence, while user-driven compactAfter context reset on approval is supported

TypeScript plan_reflection_started/resolved/stopped WS events are scoped to the asynchronous planReflectionAutoApprove loop; Go does not emit plan_reflection_* and instead exposes the explicit permission_request/permission_resolved approval flow as the supported frontend contract
blocking compact creates a compact marker message and clears provider/prune state
segment compact hides selected refs behind a compact marker and exposes summary/messages routes
context clear uses the same compact marker contract

compact route, segment compact, clear context, and context-overflow compact paths broadcast the actual TypeScript/frontend lifecycle events compacting, compact_done, and compact_failed; the previously tracked compact_progress label is not a TypeScript event name
when no caller summary is provided, Go backend builds a deterministic fallback summary instead of invoking a model

fallbacks.reason: TS-equivalent model-generated compaction is not implemented in go_backend; summaries are caller-provided or deterministic from refs.

contracts.frontendConsumerPolicy: NarratorPanel consumes compact capability through useNarratorCompactCapability, blocks unsupported compact requests before calling the API, and warns when Go compact uses caller-provided or deterministic fallback summaries instead of TypeScript model-generated summaries; MessageBubble exposes segment compact summary UI on compact markers.

features: retry trims assistant/tool results after the latest user message and returns deletedMessageIds
continue appends a Continue. user message
interrupt clears active status and preserves manual_override state needed for retry/recovery
subagent conclusion update can rewrite parent tool result from the child final assistant text
rollback truncates narrator_message_refs and assistant blocks, invalidates affected tool calls, and optionally rebuilds file state from snapshots via revert=true

edit-and-regenerate performs copy-on-write user message edits, preserves attachment block order, optionally rolls back file state, optionally skips agent rerun, deletes following messages, and broadcasts WS updates
provider-specific retryable error codes and failover metadata are preserved on raw WS events and final narrator_error payloads
agent error persistence failures emit diagnostic fallback events and stop before unsafe follow-up mutations when error-message persistence fails
background agent run completion failures emit diagnostic fallback events when the parent background task record cannot be finalized
remainingParityRisks: broader TS-vs-Go fixture comparison is still needed for remaining provider/runtime streams beyond the OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic, Kiro, NKP, NUG, Codex, and Cline provider executable fixtures; compact-boundary long-tool-chain edit/regenerate behavior, provider-specific retryable error diagnostics, failure compensation paths, provider invalidState fixture parity, Codex rebuild-history failover parity, and core provider stream/body/header fixture parity are now covered by focused Go contract tests

features: Agent tool creates foreground and background subagent narrators
background subagents are tracked in background_tasks and emit P1 background events
Await supports type=agent and returns stable unsupported metadata for other task types
Send and TeamStatus support list, send, broadcast, and file_changes across accessible sibling subagents
explore and review subagents default to readOnly permission; plan subagents enter plan mode
custom subagent types are stored, with fallback prompts when custom prompt files are unavailable

fallbacks.reason: Go backend can mark background/foreground state but cannot re-block an already-running parent tool promise after detach/attach.

contracts.frontendConsumerPolicy: SubagentCard and BackgroundTasksDrawer gate foreground/background, detach/open-session, cancel, and stale-recovery actions through subagent capability metadata; BackgroundTasksDrawer surfaces reattach fallback warnings so users do not assume a detached parent tool promise can be re-blocked after attach.

features: /api/mcp/tools lists Go compatibility tools
MCP JSON-RPC initialize and tools/list are supported
MCP JSON-RPC tools/call dispatches embedded NarraFork compatibility tools
MCP server definitions are persisted through settings.json when a settings store is present
stdio MCP server probing can discover external tools for metadata
connected stdio MCP tools are injected into Go narrator provider tool lists with per-call stdio JSON-RPC execution
frontend tool permissions surface partial MCP agent-injection parity warnings

fallbacks.reason: SSE and streamable HTTP MCP transports remain metadata/configuration only; only connected stdio MCP tools are executable by Go narrator agents.

contracts.frontendConsumerPolicy: tool-permissions surfaces partial stdio MCP agent-injection parity and non-stdio fallback reasons before users assume all external MCP transports are executable by Go agents.

features: review tool scope includes ConcludeReview without leaking into normal tool scope
ConcludeReview validates review chapter state and persists review_conclusions in TS-compatible shape
ConcludeReview updates review_status to concluded and injects review feedback into the source narrator
review promote, dismiss, and convert-to-subagent compatibility routes expose stable closure actions
chapter merge rejects stale review conclusions when the reviewed source has moved
